analysis.evidence: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם means “whoever sheds human blood.” The following clause דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed,” echoes the verb in the passive and confirms the bloodshed sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, with no prefix or suffix. It functions substantivally and takes דַּם הָאָדָם as its object.

analysis.evidence: שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם means “one who sheds human blood.” The answering clause דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “his blood shall be shed,” holds the killer accountable for the death.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state, with הָאָדָם as its genitive complement.
analysis.sense: Bloodshed in the taking of a human life.

analysis.evidence: In שֹׁפֵךְ דַּם הָאָדָם, “whoever sheds the blood of a human being,” הָאָדָם identifies the person whose blood is shed. The rule applies to any human victim.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ־ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun. The article is generic here.
analysis.sense: a man, a human being; anyone

analysis.evidence: In בָּאָדָם דָּמוֹ יִשָּׁפֵךְ, “by a human being his blood shall be shed,” בָּאָדָם identifies the human agent who sheds the blood of the person described in the opening clause.
analysis.morphology: The prefix בָּ combines the preposition בְּ with the definite article. אָדָם is a masculine singular absolute noun. The article is generic here.
analysis.sense: a man, a human being; anyone

analysis.evidence: The verse pairs active שֹׁפֵךְ ‘one who sheds’ with passive יִשָּׁפֵךְ ‘shall be shed’. The subject of the passive verb is דָּמוֹ ‘his blood’, the blood of the person who shed human blood.
analysis.morphology: Niphal imperfect, third person masculine singular, agreeing with דָּמוֹ ‘his blood’. The initial י marks the imperfect, and the Niphal נ assimilates to שׁ.

analysis.evidence: כִּי introduces the reason for the preceding judgment about shedding human blood: God made humankind in his image.
analysis.morphology: Causal conjunction without a prefix or suffix.
Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular agreement.
